stem:
Meena is helping her grandmother in the kitchen. They have a bowl of wheat grains mixed with some small stones and a few pieces of husk. Her grandmother wants to remove the unwanted pieces before grinding the wheat.

In which situation is handpicking the most suitable method of separation?

options.text: When the mixture contains a very large quantity of tiny sand particles spread evenly through the wheat.
When the unwanted pieces are few in number and large enough to be seen clearly and picked out by hand.
When the unwanted material is dissolved in water along with the useful material.
When one solid in the mixture is attracted by a magnet and the other is not.

teacher.key_rationale: Handpicking is suitable only when the components of a solid mixture are few, easily visible, and differ in size, colour, or shape so they can be picked out by hand. Option A needs sieving (too many fine particles), C needs evaporation, and D needs magnetic separation, so B is the key.
